sources.label: Waverley Council - Festival of the Winds 2026
Australian Kiteflyers Society - Bondi Festival of the Winds

blocks.text: Festival of the Winds 2026 is on Sunday 13 September 2026, from 11am to 4pm, on Bondi Beach and in Bondi Park. Entry is free and there is no ticket - you just turn up. It is run by Waverley Council with the Australian Kiteflyers Society, and it is the day the sky above Bondi fills with giant handmade kites. My one piece of advice: come by bus, and come early.

items.label: Where
items.value: Bondi Beach and Bondi Park, Campbell Parade

items.label: Run by
items.value: Waverley Council with the Australian Kiteflyers Society

items.label: Best for
items.value: Families, photographers, anyone who likes a spectacle

blocks.text: What actually happens on the day

This is not a paddock full of supermarket kites. The Australian Kiteflyers Society brings out display kites the size of small aircraft - octopuses with streaming tentacles, huge geometric box kites, creatures that take several people to launch and then hang over the beach like they are painted on the sky. Alongside them you get the fast stuff: stunt kites cutting figure-eights, and intricate handmade pieces that people have spent months building.

Around the kites, the park turns into a festival. Expect live performances, music and dancing, roaming performers working the crowd, food stalls, cultural activities, and hands-on kite-making workshops aimed at kids and families. The programme varies year to year, so if there is a specific act or workshop you want, check the council's event page closer to the day.

items: **Giant display kites** from the Australian Kiteflyers Society - the reason most people come.
**Stunt kite flying** - the fast, noisy, low-level stuff, usually the most fun to watch.
**Kite-making workshops** for children and families, hands-on.
**Live music, dancing and roaming performers** through Bondi Park.
**Food stalls** and cultural activities across the park.

blocks.text: Getting there: this is the day not to drive

Bondi has limited parking on an ordinary Sunday. On festival day, with a beach full of people and a park full of stalls, the metered bays and side streets fill early and some roads around the beach can be affected. I have watched people circle Campbell Parade for forty minutes on far quieter days than this one. Take the bus.

Only two bus routes serve Bondi Beach: the **333** and the **380**. The 333 runs from Circular Quay through the city and Bondi Junction to North Bondi, and takes roughly 40-45 minutes end to end (checked against the Transport for NSW trip planner, August 2026); it also runs 24 hours, so getting home late is never a problem. The 380 runs between Watsons Bay and Bondi Junction via the beach. If you are coming by train, the nearest station is **Bondi Junction** on the T4 line - there is no train at the beach itself, and no ferry to Bondi - then it is a 333 or 380 down the hill, or a 25-30 minute downhill walk if the buses are packed.

Tap on and off with any contactless card, phone or watch; it costs the same as an Opal card. Note that a tapped bank card always charges the adult fare, so children need their own Child Opal card to get the child fare. Check [transportnsw.info](https://transportnsw.info) for times on the day, and for any service changes around the event.

blocks.title: Check road closures before you leave
blocks.text: Waverley Council publishes any road closures, parking restrictions and transport changes for the festival on its own event page. I am not going to guess at them here - they are set close to the day and they change. Check the [council's Festival of the Winds page](https://www.waverley.nsw.gov.au/recreation/events/events/festival_of_the_winds_2026) the day before.
Where to stand, and when to arrive

The grass of Bondi Park, on the rise above the sand, is the best seat in the house. You get the whole sky in one view, the kites are above you rather than in front of you, and you are next to the food and the toilets. Get there before midday with a picnic rug and claim a patch - by early afternoon the good ground is gone. If you want photographs, the south end gives you kites with the Icebergs pool and the headland in frame.
The Sunday markets are on the same day

Here is the bit most event listings miss. Festival of the Winds falls on a Sunday, and the **Bondi Markets run every Sunday from 10am to 4pm** at Bondi Beach Public School on Campbell Parade - the fashion, vintage and design market, a two-minute walk from the festival. The hours overlap almost exactly. If you are making a day of it, do the markets first when they open at 10am, then cross to the park as the kites go up at 11am. Two events, one bus trip.
This is genuinely one of the best family days on the Bondi calendar, and it is free, which is rarer than it should be. A few practical things worth knowing before you go.

items: **Bring sunscreen and hats.** September is spring here and the UV is already strong, cloudy or not. Reapply.
**Water is free.** There are refill bubblers along the promenade and Sydney tap water is fine to drink.
**Toilets, showers and change rooms** are in the Bondi Pavilion in the middle of the beachfront, open 6am-10pm daily, with baby-change facilities.
**Bring your own kite if you have one.** Plenty of families fly their own alongside the display kites - just keep well clear of the big society kites and their lines.
**No dogs.** Dogs are not allowed on Bondi Beach or the promenade at any time, festival or not.
**No alcohol and no glass.** Bondi Beach and Bondi Park are an enforced alcohol-free, glass-free zone. There are free public BBQs in Bondi Park if you want to cook.

blocks.text: I like that this one is a genuinely local story. Festival of the Winds first took flight in 1978, started by a small group of Sydney kite enthusiasts who worked out that a wide beach with a reliable spring breeze was close to a perfect kite ground. It grew, Waverley Council got behind it, and the Australian Kiteflyers Society brought the giant handmade display kites that turned it from a picnic into a spectacle. Nearly fifty years on it is billed by its organisers as Australia's premier kite festival, and it still has the feel of a community day rather than a corporate one.

items.q: When is Festival of the Winds 2026?
items.a: Sunday 13 September 2026. The festival is traditionally held on the second Sunday of September each year at Bondi Beach.

items.q: What time does Festival of the Winds start and finish?
items.a: 11am to 4pm. Arrive before midday if you want a good patch of grass in Bondi Park - the best spots go early.

items.q: Is Festival of the Winds free?
items.a: Yes. Entry is free and there is no ticket or registration - you simply turn up. Food and anything you buy from the stalls costs money, but the festival itself does not.

items.q: Where exactly is Festival of the Winds held?
items.a: On Bondi Beach and in Bondi Park, along Campbell Parade in Bondi Beach, with activities spreading through the park and around the Bondi Pavilion.

items.q: Can I bring my own kite?
items.a: Yes, and lots of families do. Keep well away from the Australian Kiteflyers Society's large display kites and their lines, which need a lot of clear space and can carry serious force.

items.q: Can I bring my dog to Festival of the Winds?
items.a: No. Dogs are not permitted on Bondi Beach or the promenade at any time, including during the festival. Bondi Park and the beach are also an enforced alcohol-free and glass-free zone.

items.q: Is there parking at Festival of the Winds?
items.a: Parking around Bondi is metered, limited and fills very early on festival day, and the council may set restrictions or closures close to the event. Take the 333 or 380 bus, or the T4 train to Bondi Junction and a bus down. Check the council's event page for the day's traffic arrangements.

items.q: What happens if the weather is bad?
items.a: It is an outdoor festival on a beach, so conditions matter. Waverley Council posts any cancellation or change on its Festival of the Winds page - check there on the morning if the forecast looks poor.

blocks.text: So: Sunday 13 September 2026, 11am to 4pm, free, on the bus, with a rug and sunscreen. If you are building the rest of the day around it, the [Bondi Markets on a Sunday](/whats-on/bondi-markets-sunday) are a two-minute walk away, my [Bondi with kids guide](/bondi-with-kids) covers the playgrounds and the calmest swimming, and [what's on at Bondi](/whats-on) lists the rest of the year's events.
